topics.title: The Hidden Politics of Money
topics.description: Why central banks are never as independent as they claim — and what the history of inflation tells us about who really controls the dollar. A tour of monetary policy that connects the headlines to the institutions behind them.
topics.audience: General audiences, policy forums, donor events

topics.title: Sound Money and the Case for Rules
topics.description: What economic history reveals about the costs of discretionary monetary policy, and why predictable rules tend to outperform good intentions. Accessible to non-economists, grounded in the research.

topics.title: Public Choice: Economics Without Romance
topics.description: Politicians and bureaucrats respond to incentives like everyone else. A practical introduction to how public-choice economics explains policy outcomes most people find baffling.

topics.title: Reading the Economy Behind the Headlines
topics.description: A working economist's guide to making sense of inflation, interest rates, and the news cycle — separating signal from noise without the jargon.
